purpose: Execution status for the four bounded high-yield tasks selected after the global archive sweep. This is a research status file, not a public progress counter. Naples row 383 has now been revisited against the locally held primary OCR and closed at catalogue-offering level.

targets.target: St Andrews — Charles Elcock letters, 6–8 March 1884
targets.result: Exact archive locator closed at ms21974-ms21975. The catalogue explicitly states that the correspondence refers to Challenger expedition samples, while also identifying antiquarian/medal discussion as the main theme. The decisive Challenger passage itself is not transcribed in the indexed record, so sender/sample/station/purpose remain open until page images are obtained.
targets.grade: S archive locator; A+/S-candidate content bridge
targets.next_bounded_action: Obtain/transcribe ms21974-ms21975 only; no broad St Andrews search needed.

Full 4,723-row spreadsheet harvest was not possible in this runtime because the binary resource was not retrieved.

targets.target: Naples catalogue row 383 ↔ St Andrews Delphinus phocaena BPM/1/T8/6
targets.result: The locally held primary catalogue OCR on printed p.253 directly gives 382 Delphinus phocaena L. Milz, 383 ditto Penis, 384 ditto Hode and 385 ditto Niere. Offering 383 is therefore Delphinus phocaena L., Penis. The surviving St Andrews slide independently carries Stazione Zoologica Napoli labels, taxon Delphinus phocaena and right-label public transcription 'Panis 383'. Station + taxon + exact number closes the slide as an extant instance corresponding to catalogue offering 383; the Panis/Penis discrepancy remains explicit.
targets.grade: S/A++ catalogue-offering identity; individual-copy production/shipment history open
targets.next_bounded_action: No further web search. Inspect the object image only if resolving Panis/Penis handwriting matters, or a page image only if the row price is needed.

net_result: Balfour produced an S-level publication/instrument-designation closure; Challenger produced an S-level address architecture plus diagnostic object harvest; Elcock is narrowed to two exact letters; Naples 383 is now closed at catalogue-offering-to-surviving-object level from the local primary source. None of the remaining open edges justifies renewed broad discovery.
methodological_note: Preserve the distinction between a catalogue offering and a unique physical serial object. The Naples closure identifies BPM/1/T8/6 with offering 383, not with a uniquely dated production batch or specific shipment copy.
